vsam.why: base/cntl/adef121.jcl DEFINE1: DATA(... KEYS(10 0) RECORDSIZE(225 225)); the engine's facts do not read KEYS / RECORDSIZE inside the DATA component, so the case states them

notes: GenApp's VSAM 'customer key range' inquiry (LGICVS01, transaction LGCF in the CSD, a terminal transaction: no program LINKs it). It reads TS queue GENACNTL (ITEM(1), then NEXT until ITEMERR) for the 'LOW CUSTOMER=' / 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' items GenApp's LGSETUP writes, takes a key = INTEGER(RANDOM(EIBTASKN) * (HIGH - LOW) + LOW), and EXEC CICS READ FILE('KSDSCUST') INTO(CA-AREA) LENGTH(F82 = 225) RIDFLD(WRITE-MSG-HIGH) KEYLENGTH(F10 = 10) GTEQ (#4270, oracle_assumptions.md X22): the key itself when on file, else the first greater key; NOTFND past the last. On NORMAL the record's number replaces the key; SEND TEXT FROM(WRITE-MSG-H) LENGTH(24) then shows 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' and the 10 bytes after it in WRITE-MSG (a LENGTH past FROM, inside its record). Facts stated on both sides: STARTCODE 'TD' (a terminal task, X19), the terminal's input 'LGCF' (an unformatted RECEIVE), the queue GENACNTL as LGSETUP leaves it, EIBTASKN (X21), the region (ASSIGN SYSID, unused after). Queue-shape scenarios (queue-empty, queue-header-only, queue-low-only, queue-high-only): a queue with a missing item makes the program WRITEQ 'LOW CUSTOMER=' / 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' FROM(WRITE-MSG-L / -H) X(13) / X(14) LENGTH(23) / (24), past its FROM item (X6: written padded, FROM's bytes then spaces, ASSUMED on both sides), so each task is compared whole. They reach the ReadQ-not-NORMAL and the LOW / HIGH not-found sides. Not exercised: the COMMAREA path (a START with data, or LINKed), which no GenApp program takes. Data: ksdscust.txt holds the ten GenApp sample customers of genapp-lgucvs01 plus two SYNTHETIC ones (0001000005, 0001000009: details copied from customer 1) so a key between them and past the last exists. Derived from the CICS General Insurance Application (GenApp, github.com/cicsdev/cics-genapp; (C) Copyright IBM Corp. 2011, 2020), licensed under the Eclipse Public License 2.0: LICENSE here is the corpus's own, NOTICE names the source and what was derived.

region.why: a deployment fact: LGICVS01 ASSIGNs SYSID (unused afterwards); GenApp names no region in the corpus

scenarios.name: gteq-key-on-file
scenarios.why: LOW = HIGH = 3: the key is 0000000003, on file; READ GTEQ reads it (NORMAL) and SEND TEXT shows HIGH CUSTOMER=0000000003

scenarios.name: gteq-next-key
scenarios.why: the key 0000000011 is not on file: GTEQ reads the first greater key, 0001000005 (NORMAL), and its number is sent

scenarios.name: gteq-past-the-end
scenarios.why: no key >= 0002000000: NOTFND (RESP2 80); WRITE-MSG-HIGH keeps the key asked for

scenarios.name: gteq-random-in-range
scenarios.why: LOW 1, HIGH 10: the key is FUNCTION RANDOM(EIBTASKN) scaled into the range (C12, X21), read by GTEQ

scenarios.name: queue-empty
scenarios.why: no GENACNTL queue: the first ReadQ is not NORMAL, WS-FLAG-TSQE stays 'Y' and the E, L and H records are all written; LOW = HIGH = 0001000001 (the program's defaults), the key is read by GTEQ

scenarios.name: queue-header-only
scenarios.why: GENACNTL holds only the header item: the first ReadQ is NORMAL (TSQE cleared) but no LOW CUSTOMER or HIGH CUSTOMER item follows, so the L and H records are written; LOW = HIGH = 0001000001

scenarios.name: queue-low-only
scenarios.why: no HIGH CUSTOMER item: LOW is taken from the queue, HIGH keeps its default, so only the H record is written; the key is scaled into LOW..HIGH

scenarios.name: queue-high-only
scenarios.why: no LOW CUSTOMER item: HIGH is taken from the queue, LOW keeps its default, so only the L record is written; the key is scaled into LOW..HIGH

scenarios.name: dpl-start-on-terminal-case
scenarios.why: STARTCODE D (a distributed program link, not a terminal start): WS-FLAG is 'C', the RECEIVE is skipped and the key goes back in COMMA-DATA with no SEND TEXT; the other arm of the STARTCODE test than the terminal scenarios take
